title: release.decide is published human-only and opens a proof-carrying pull request
description:
SPIDR child 2 of task-2a345b2e97d94599b4688af1923056e5 (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). dependsOn child 1 task-70a7ccd3293f465fbc9c1888ae540f5d for the dossier bytes this row puts in the PR body.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the command kind with its roster backfill and refusal codes, and the PR-opening port plus the release receipt. No UI - that is child 3.

ARCHITECT DECISION on the question the parent row left open ("`gh pr create` on the operator's machine, or the REST API with a token the human names on the goal - architect decides"): USE THE `gh` CLI. Reasons, so it is not re-litigated: (1) a per-goal API token is SECRET HANDLING, and the parent's rail 2 is FEATURES ONLY with security-boundary work out of scope - storing, redacting and rotating a token is exactly that work; (2) the daemon already spawns workspace commands as child processes with timeouts and process-group cleanup (orchestrator/verifier-process-runner.ts), so `gh` needs no new mechanism; (3) the operator's machine already holds the git credentials the publisher pushes with, so `gh` inherits an auth story that exists rather than inventing a second one. `gh` absent or unauthenticated REFUSES CLEANLY with RELEASE_PR_FAILED carrying the tool's last stderr line - it does not fall back to a token path.

ROSTER, traced from an existing human-only decide kind (`escalation.decide`): daemon-command-vocabulary.ts (kind, capability, family, PAYLOAD_KEYS, OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS), daemon-command-families.ts (the per-kind flag block), daemon-command-registry.ts (`entryOf` resolves asyncEntries then family flags), mcp-tool-allowlist.ts (EXCLUDED), packages/contracts/src/runtime/runtime-vocabulary.ts, and the GENERATED client (`pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client generate` - never hand-edited; it pins GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST, checked at client-compat.ts:169).

TWO PAYLOAD-KEY TEST TABLES must both gain a row and are invisible to a grep for the kind literal in production source: daemon-command-vocabulary.test.ts (~:170-182) and daemon-command-registry.test.ts (~:197-203, plus the flat roster ~:283-300). Measured the hard way on task-4b9c394d, where neither the plan nor a governor triage named them.

HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS has exactly ONE definition (agent-spawn-contract.ts:195); agent-wrapper.ts:24 re-exports it. Do not look for a second.
definitionOfDone: `release.decide` published human-only and MCP-EXCLUDED with the full roster backfill, and a BIDIRECTIONAL set-equality test that enumerates the SERVED kinds from the dispatch seam and asserts equality with the advertised roster in both directions - a test iterating the roster constant alone sees only one direction. Verify by deleting the entry from each side in turn and confirming both go red.

The three refusal codes carry a closed code->layer map (the refusal factory takes no layer argument, so a call site cannot mint a disagreeing pair) and each is asserted with code AND layer: RELEASE_REMOTE_MISSING; RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE, whose detail NAMES THE MISSING CRITERIA (assert the criterion ids appear - 'evidence incomplete' without naming what is missing sends the operator hunting); RELEASE_PR_FAILED, carrying the tool's LAST STDERR LINE verbatim.

PR creation goes through an injectable port so it is tested OFFLINE: the request (title, base, head, body) is asserted BYTE-FOR-BYTE, with body equal to child 1's dossier bytes - not a re-rendered copy, since a second rendering is how the PR body and the stored dossier come to differ.

`gh` absent, unauthenticated, or failing refuses RELEASE_PR_FAILED with its stderr line and commits NO release receipt claiming success - assert the store holds no RELEASED receipt on that path. A refused release that recorded success is the worst possible outcome here.

`moe-release-receipt/1` records {goalId, sha, dossierSha256, prUrl, RELEASED|REFUSED(code)}, mirroring repository/landing-receipt-contracts.ts; a REFUSED receipt carries its code and NO prUrl. Read it back from a real store and assert every member.

APPROVE reuses the EXISTING publisher to push (orchestrator/node-publisher.ts) rather than a second push path; assert the push happened through it, and that a goal whose remote is unbound refuses RELEASE_REMOTE_MISSING before anything is pushed.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` (packages/contracts and the generated client are touched, so the root lane is real evidence here).
taskRails: `gh` CLI ONLY - no token path, no REST fallback. A per-goal token is secret handling and the parent's FEATURES ONLY rail puts it out of scope. Absent or unauthenticated `gh` refuses cleanly.

NEVER HAND-EDIT the generated client: run `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room-client generate` and quote the OLD and NEW GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST. A hand-typed entry passes every grep and fails the runtime compat check.
REUSE THE PUBLISHER for the push (orchestrator/node-publisher.ts). A second push path is how the two come to disagree about what was pushed.
The PR body IS child 1's stored dossier bytes, not a fresh rendering. If they can differ, the PR stops being proof-carrying.
FEATURES ONLY (inherited): no security-boundary or policy work.

implementationPlan.description: RE-MEASURE THE DELIVERED TREE. READ-ONLY - this step writes nothing, so it declares no affected files. (a) Confirm children A and B landed the vocabulary this row consumes: `git grep -n 'release\.decide' -- apps packages` must now hit, and `grep -n 'RELEASE_REMOTE_MISSING\|RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE\|RELEASE_PR_FAILED' apps/daemon/src/release/release-decide-contracts.ts` must show all three codes plus the frozen code->layer map and the code-only refusal factory. If any is absent, moe.report_blocked with blockedOnTaskIds naming task-bda0eeac02544c1992c6738c2db83178 / task-54b74b8041c64bc2868435bcbdac6dd6 - do NOT re-declare the codes here, a second declaration is exactly the disagreeing pair the closed map exists to prevent. (b) Read the surfaces this row composes, all measured present at plan time: `readReleaseDossier(store, projectId, dossierId)` and `releaseDossierId(projectId, goalId, sha)` (release-dossier-ledger.ts:70 / release-dossier-contracts.ts:153); `readProjectRemote(store, projectId): ProjectRemote | null` (repository/publish-ledger.ts:135); `readPublishLedger` (:84) and `PublishReceiptV1 {branch, sha, remoteUrl, url, outcome}` (repository/publish-receipt-contracts.ts:41); `createNodePublisher({clock, git, projectId, store, workspace}).publishOnce()` (orchestrator/node-publisher.ts:35); `createVerifierProcessRunner` and its RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS allow-list posture (orchestrator/verifier-process-runner.ts:31) as the reference for spawning a child process with a timeout. (c) Run `grep -rn 'release-dossier' apps/daemon/src/index-surface.test.ts apps/daemon/src/index.ts` to learn whether adding an export to release-dossier.ts moves a barrel or export-count roster; if it does, STOP and report it rather than taking the extra path - the architect amends. Record every command and its result in the step note.

ONE DERIVATION OF THE GAPS, exported. `ReleaseDossierV1` stores ONLY `{dossierId, goalId, markdown, projectId, sha, version}` (measured, release-dossier-contracts.ts:98) - the criterion rows are NOT in the record, so RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE cannot name the missing criteria by reading the stored bytes, and re-parsing the markdown back into rows would be authority reimplemented against a document. Instead extract the EXISTING private row pipeline in release-dossier.ts (`rowOf` over sorted `input.criteria`, memoized ancestry) into a new exported `releaseDossierGaps(input: DossierInput, sha: string, ancestry: AncestryPredicate): readonly DossierGap[]`, and have `renderReleaseDossier` CALL it so exactly one derivation exists - a second copy is how the PR body and the refusal come to disagree about what is missing. Pure and sync: do NOT make it async (child 1's QA settled that `AncestryPredicate` is sync on purpose so the core stays byte-deterministic and fakeable). Re-run child 1's suite unchanged - `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json src/release` from apps/daemon - and quote its `Test Files N passed` line: the 30 existing tests must stay green with no edit to release-dossier.test.ts.

THE RELEASE RECEIPT, contract half. New `release-receipt-contracts.ts`, mirroring repository/landing-receipt-contracts.ts (its `exact()` key-roster decode, null-prototype object guard and sha256 id derivation) and release-dossier-contracts.ts. Declare `RELEASE_RECEIPT_VERSION = 'moe-release-receipt/1'`, `RELEASE_RECEIPT_COMMAND_KIND = 'internal.release.receipt'`, `RELEASE_RECEIPT_PRINCIPAL_ID = 'daemon:release'`, `ReleaseReceiptV1 {dossierSha256, goalId, outcome: 'RELEASED'|'REFUSED', prUrl: string|null, projectId, receiptId, refusalCode: ReleaseRefusalCode|null, sha, version}` and `decodeReleaseReceiptBytes`. THE TWO STRUCTURAL INVARIANTS, enforced in the decoder rather than by convention: a RELEASED receipt has a non-null `prUrl` and a null `refusalCode`; a REFUSED receipt has a null `prUrl` and a non-null `refusalCode` drawn from the closed code set in release-decide-contracts.ts. `dossierSha256` is the sha256 of the STORED markdown bytes (the same bytes that become the PR body), so a reader can bind a receipt to the exact evidence document. Reuse `releaseDossierAggregateId(goalId)` - the receipt lands on the goal's release aggregate beside the dossier, never on the goal.

THE RELEASE RECEIPT, durable half. New `release-receipt-ledger.ts`, mirroring release-dossier-ledger.ts line for line: `recordReleaseReceipt(store, input)` writes through `commitExpectedVersionDecision` under RELEASE_RECEIPT_PRINCIPAL_ID with a replay-on-existing path (same id => `{ok:true, replayed:true}`, never a second append), and `readReleaseReceipt(store, projectId, receiptId)` re-validates the decision against the bytes it carries and answers `{code:'RELEASE_RECEIPT_NOT_FOUND'|'RELEASE_RECEIPT_INVALID', ok:false}`. Same `ownDecision` try/catch shape - a store read that throws answers INVALID rather than escaping. Keep the file under 250 physical lines.

RECEIPT TESTS against a REAL store, not a fake. New `release-receipt-ledger.test.ts` using the same in-repo SqliteEventStore fixture release-dossier-ledger.test.ts uses. Arms: (1) record a RELEASED receipt, READ IT BACK and assert EVERY member individually - goalId, sha, dossierSha256, prUrl, outcome, refusalCode null, version - not a single toStrictEqual against an object built from the same literals; (2) record a REFUSED receipt per code and assert `refusalCode` is that exact code AND `prUrl` is null; (3) the decoder REFUSES a forged RELEASED-with-null-prUrl and a forged REFUSED-with-a-prUrl, asserted by the returned code, and refuses an unknown refusalCode not in the closed set; (4) re-recording the same id replays with `replayed:true` and appends no second event (assert the event count on the aggregate before and after). Mutation drill on the decoder's RELEASED/REFUSED invariant, quoted red.

THE gh PR PORT, injectable and tested OFFLINE. New `release-pr-port.ts` exporting `interface ReleasePrRequest {base, body, head, title}`, `type ReleasePrResult = {ok:true, prUrl} | {ok:false, stderrLastLine, spawnErrorCode: string|null}`, `interface ReleasePrPort { open(request): Promise<ReleasePrResult> }` and `createGhReleasePrPort({cwd, spawn?, timeoutMs?})`. gh CLI ONLY - no token path, no REST fallback (task rail 1). MECHANICS, all decided here so they are not re-derived: argv array with `shell:false` (`['pr','create','--base',base,'--head',head,'--title',title,'--body-file',<temp path>]`); executable is the bare name `gh` - Windows CreateProcess appends `.exe` for an extension-less name, so do NOT hard-code `gh.exe` or `gh.cmd`, and do NOT set shell:true. The BODY GOES IN A TEMP FILE, never in argv: a dossier is multi-kilobyte markdown and Windows caps a command line at 32767 chars, so an argv body would truncate the evidence silently. The temp file is removed in a `finally` on EVERY exit path including timeout and spawn error. stdout is trimmed to its last non-empty line as `prUrl`; stderr is retained tail-bounded and reduced to its LAST NON-EMPTY line. A spawn that never starts (gh absent => ENOENT) has NO stderr: answer `{ok:false, stderrLastLine:'', spawnErrorCode:'ENOENT'}` so the caller can still say something true. A timeout kills the child and answers ok:false. Non-zero exit (unauthenticated gh) answers ok:false with the real last stderr line.

PR PORT TESTS, fully offline via the injected `spawn`. New `release-pr-port.test.ts`. Arms: (1) HAPPY - assert the spawned argv BYTE FOR BYTE (exact array equality, including flag order) and assert the file named by `--body-file` contains EXACTLY the body string passed in, byte for byte, read inside the fake spawn before it resolves; assert prUrl is the last stdout line. (2) gh ABSENT - the fake spawn emits an `error` event with `code:'ENOENT'`; assert `{ok:false, spawnErrorCode:'ENOENT'}`. (3) gh UNAUTHENTICATED - exit 1 with multi-line stderr; assert `stderrLastLine` is the LAST NON-EMPTY line verbatim, not the first and not the whole blob. (4) TIMEOUT - assert the child is killed and the call settles ok:false. (5) CLEANUP - after every one of the four arms above, assert the temp body file NO LONGER EXISTS. Assert cross-platform argv: the recipe must be identical on win32 and posix (drive the port with an injected platform if the implementation reads one).

THE DECIDE SERVICE. New `release-decide-service.ts` exporting `createReleaseDecideHandler({clock, dossierFacts, prPort, projectId, publisher, store})` where `publisher` is exactly `createNodePublisher(...)`'s return shape `{publishOnce}` - REUSE THE EXISTING PUBLISHER, never a second push path (task rail 3). ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING, and each refusal returns a code from the closed map with NO layer argument: (1) `readProjectRemote(store, projectId)` === null => RELEASE_REMOTE_MISSING, refused BEFORE anything is pushed and before any receipt is written. (2) `releaseDossierGaps(...)` non-empty => RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE whose detail NAMES THE CRITERION IDS (sorted, joined) - 'evidence incomplete' without naming what is missing sends the operator hunting. (3) `readReleaseDossier(store, projectId, releaseDossierId(projectId, goalId, sha))` not ok => RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE naming the absent dossier record. (4) `await publisher.publishOnce()`, then read the goal's PublishReceiptV1 from `readPublishLedger`; no PUSHED receipt => RELEASE_PR_FAILED carrying the publisher's refusal detail (the PR cannot be opened because the head was never pushed - this stays inside the closed three-code set rather than minting a fourth). (5) `prPort.open({base, body: <the STORED dossier.markdown bytes, verbatim>, head: receipt.branch, title})` - the body is the stored bytes, NEVER a fresh render (task rail 4). (6) On ok: record a RELEASED receipt with prUrl and `dossierSha256` over the stored markdown. On !ok: RELEASE_PR_FAILED carrying `stderrLastLine` verbatim (or the spawn error code when there was no stderr) and record a REFUSED receipt with that code and NO prUrl. A REJECT decision records a REFUSED receipt and never pushes and never opens a PR. The payload this handler decodes is caller INTENT ONLY - {base, decision, goalId, sha}; projectId, principalId, correlationId and decidedAt are SERVER facts the registry re-attaches. Keep the file under 250 physical lines; split if it grows.

SERVICE TESTS, offline, against a real store with fake prPort/publisher. New `release-decide-service.test.ts`. Every refusal arm asserts the CODE AND the LAYER the closed map resolves - never merely that it did not succeed. Arms: (1) unbound remote => RELEASE_REMOTE_MISSING, and assert `publisher.publishOnce` was called ZERO times and `prPort.open` zero times - refused BEFORE anything is pushed. (2) a criterion with a gap => RELEASE_EVIDENCE_INCOMPLETE whose detail CONTAINS each missing criterion id (assert the ids, not the sentence). (3) HAPPY => `prPort.open` received a request whose `body` is IDENTICAL (===, not merely equal-looking) to the markdown read back out of the store by `readReleaseDossier`, asserted against the store read and not against a literal; and the whole request {base, head, title, body} asserted byte for byte. (4) gh ABSENT / UNAUTHENTICATED / FAILING => RELEASE_PR_FAILED carrying the stderr last line verbatim, AND read the store back and assert it holds NO receipt whose outcome is RELEASED for that goal - a refused release that recorded success is the worst outcome here, so assert the absence positively rather than trusting the return value. (5) push refused => RELEASE_PR_FAILED, `prPort.open` never called. (6) assert `publisher.publishOnce` was called EXACTLY once on the approve path, and grep the service source for git-port imports to prove no second push path exists. MUTATION DRILLS, each quoted red: swap the order of the remote check and the push (arm 1 must red); change one code's entry in the closed map (the code-AND-layer arms must red); return a freshly rendered markdown instead of the stored bytes (arm 3 must red). Restore proof per global rail 13: `git status --porcelain` the mutated paths BEFORE drilling, and because every module in this row is UNTRACKED (`??`), prove each restore by SHA256 equality against an out-of-tree backup under %TEMP% suffixed by worker id, in a call SEPARATE from the restore - `git diff` is blind to untracked paths and certifies nothing here.

WIRE THE HANDLER, replacing child B's fail-closed stub. In `daemon-command-async-entries.ts`, swap the `release.decide` stub for `createReleaseDecideHandler(...)`, composing `prPort` as `createGhReleasePrPort(...)` and `publisher` as the existing `createNodePublisher(...)`. Follow the file's established posture exactly: HOST-SCOPED config is read once at the composition root and passed down RAW, absent optional keys are SPREAD not assigned (`...(x === undefined ? {} : {key: x})`) because exactOptionalPropertyTypes makes an explicit undefined a different thing from an absent key, and an unconfigured daemon REFUSES under the producer's own code rather than substituting a default. The workspace is the same one node-publisher takes; a null workspace must refuse, never push. Do not touch daemon-command-vocabulary.ts, daemon-command-families.ts, daemon-command-registry.ts, mcp-tool-allowlist.ts or agent-spawn-contract.ts - child B owns all five and they are already correct at this point.

VERIFY, then ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW. Run and QUOTE the `Test Files N passed` count line for each - an exit code alone is not evidence, and a `--filter` leg that matched no package prints no count line and still exits 0: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` (budget ~320s, measured by child 1's QA), `pnpm typecheck`, and `pnpm test` (root lane; note explicitly that it covers NO apps/** so it is evidence only for packages, per the epic rail). Attribute any red per the path-attributed-baseline rail: record repo-wide failures at the merge-base, at HEAD, and the delta intersected with this row's owned paths - report foreign red verbatim with its failing file and lines, never hidden and never fabricated green. Then invoke Skill(adversarial-self-review) and read the diff as an attacker: what if `publishOnce` resolves but the receipt read races a concurrent publish; what if the dossier markdown is empty or megabytes; what if `gh` writes the PR url to stderr instead of stdout; what if the temp body file survives a crash between spawn and finally; what if two operators dispatch release.decide for the same goal and sha concurrently (the receipt id is derived, so assert the second replays rather than double-opening a PR); what if `receipt.branch` is null on a PUSHED receipt. Fix or file each finding as a row comment before moe.complete_task.

comments.content:
SPIDR follow-on (architect-2e480458, 2026-09-05). Child B (task-54b74b80) could not carry wiring+fence in one plan: rail 18 found three extra MCP count pins (human-approver.test.ts, mcp-main.test.ts, mcp-http-host.test.ts) that push the combined roster past the 10-file hard cap.

New child: task-20b7d6bba60f445faa87a51a09d4b125 (MCP-excluded + HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS + bidirectional MCP tests). This parent now dependsOn [task-70a7ccd3, task-bda0eeac, task-54b74b80, task-20b7d6bb]. C's stub-swap in daemon-command-async-entries.ts still waits only on B's wiring landing; the fence child does not touch that file.

planSizeWarnings: Plan has 11 steps (target <=8); plans over 12 are rejected. Consider splitting the task before it grows.
Plan touches 9 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
SPLIT DECISION, and why it is not negotiable. Planned footprint measured at 21 distinct files against the daemon's 10-file HARD reject: roster backfill 13 (7 production + 6 hand-written test pins) plus 8 for the PR/receipt behaviour. Two rows cannot hold 21 either. So the row was SPIDR-split three ways and this row keeps the behaviour: child A task-bda0eeac02544c1992c6738c2db83178 (shared runtime contract, generated client, the three refusal codes and their closed code->layer map), child B task-54b74b8041c64bc2868435bcbdac6dd6 (daemon wiring, operator fence, MCP exclusion, fail-closed async entry), child C = this row. dependsOn now names both children plus task-70a7ccd3 for the dossier bytes.

GAPS DERIVATION: considered re-parsing the stored markdown back into criterion rows so nothing outside this row changes - rejected, that is authority reimplemented against a document, and it would let the PR body and the refusal disagree about what is missing. Considered passing the gap list in from the caller - rejected, same reason. Chose extracting ONE exported derivation from child 1's existing private row pipeline, with renderReleaseDossier calling it, so there is exactly one answer to 'what is missing'.

PUSH-FAILURE CODE: considered a fourth refusal code for 'pushed nothing' - rejected, the DoD names exactly three and the closed map is the point. A failed push maps to RELEASE_PR_FAILED carrying the publisher's detail: the PR genuinely cannot be opened because the head was never pushed.

PR BODY TRANSPORT: considered passing the dossier as a `--body` argv value - rejected, Windows caps a command line at 32767 chars and a multi-kilobyte dossier would truncate the evidence SILENTLY. Temp file plus `--body-file`, removed in a finally on every exit path.

gh vs a REST token: settled by the parent row, not re-litigated. gh CLI only.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT HEAD (architect-71b9a4e9, 2026-09-05, branch moe/work-2026-09-04). `git grep -n 'release\\.decide' -- apps packages adapters` => EXIT 1, ZERO hits: the kind does not exist anywhere, so nothing here re-implements a landed surface.

Child 1 (task-70a7ccd3) IS on disk and DONE: apps/daemon/src/release/ holds release-dossier{,-contracts,-ledger,-sections,-fixtures}.ts. `ReleaseDossierV1` (release-dossier-contracts.ts:98) stores ONLY {dossierId, goalId, markdown, projectId, sha, version} - the criterion rows are NOT in the record. That single fact drives step 2.

Publisher chain: `readProjectRemote(store, projectId): ProjectRemote | null` at repository/publish-ledger.ts:135 is the RELEASE_REMOTE_MISSING oracle. `createNodePublisher` (orchestrator/node-publisher.ts:35) is LEDGER-DRIVEN - `publishOnce()` walks `readPublishLedger` for requests with no receipt and pushes via `GitPublishPort`. `PublishReceiptV1` (repository/publish-receipt-contracts.ts:41) carries {branch, sha, remoteUrl, url, outcome}; `branch` is the PR head.

Process-spawn precedent: orchestrator/verifier-process-runner.ts already spawns with an env allow-list (RUNTIME_ENVIRONMENT_KEYS at :31), a default 120s timeout, a kill grace and process-group cleanup. gh needs no new mechanism.

Durable-record precedent to mirror: repository/landing-receipt-contracts.ts (exact key-roster decode, null-prototype guard, sha256 id) and release-dossier-ledger.ts (commitExpectedVersionDecision under a reserved principal, replay-on-existing, re-validate on read).

PAYLOAD SHAPE for release.decide, decided here and posted as a comment on child B so its PAYLOAD_KEYS row matches: ["base", "decision", "goalId", "sha"] - caller INTENT only; projectId, principalId, correlationId and decidedAt are SERVER facts the registry re-attaches, exactly as every other roster entry documents.

Async-entry composition rules read off daemon-command-async-entries.ts:43: host-scoped config read once at the root and passed RAW; absent optional keys SPREAD not assigned (exactOptionalPropertyTypes makes explicit undefined different from absent); an unconfigured daemon refuses under the producer's own code rather than substituting a default.
planningNotes.risks:
1. CHILDREN A AND B MAY NOT HAVE LANDED. dependsOn gates the WORKING claim, but step 1 re-verifies on disk anyway: if release-decide-contracts.ts is missing, BLOCK - do NOT declare the three codes a second time, because two declarations is precisely the disagreeing (code, layer) pair the closed map exists to prevent.

2. THE PR BODY CAN SILENTLY BECOME A SECOND RENDERING. The service must read the markdown out of the store and pass that exact string. Step 9 arm 3 asserts identity against the STORE READ, not against a literal - a literal would pass under a re-render too.

3. A REFUSED RELEASE THAT RECORDS SUCCESS is the worst outcome on this row. Assert the ABSENCE of a RELEASED receipt positively by reading the store back on every failure arm; trusting the return value proves nothing about what was written.

4. UNTRACKED-PATH DRILL RESTORES. Every module this row creates is untracked (`??`), so `git diff -- <file>` is EMPTY before, during and after a mutation and certifies NOTHING. Use `git status --porcelain` first and prove each restore by SHA256 against an out-of-tree backup, in a call SEPARATE from the restore (a PowerShell copy can silently no-op).

5. WINDOWS SPAWN. Bare `gh` with shell:false resolves to gh.exe via CreateProcess; hard-coding `gh.cmd` is the EINVAL trap the global rail records for pnpm launchers. Keep shell:false, argv arrays, no piping - a piped run reports the wrong exit status.

6. TEMP-FILE LEAK. The body file must be removed on timeout and on spawn error, not only on the happy path; step 7 asserts non-existence after all four arms.

7. CONCURRENCY. Two operators dispatching the same (goal, sha) must not open two PRs: the receipt id is derived, so the second must replay. Named explicitly in the adversarial step.

8. GATE SHAPE. `pnpm test` covers NO apps/** - it is evidence for packages only. The daemon leg is `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` and takes ~320s (measured by child 1's QA). A leg with no `Test Files N passed` count line ran nothing, whatever its exit code.
